messages:
Sam: Heads-up — after the 0.9.5 runtime deploy we observed a ~25% tail latency regression on long-context generation. I tried to profile with nsys / perfetto and ran into attach/driver noise. Copying the rough trace + failures below.
Priya: Can you paste the nsys error you hit when attaching?
Sam: Yep. This was from trying to attach to the dedicated-runtime container:
```
$ nsys attach --pid 21437 --output attach-trace.qdrep
Attaching to PID 21437...
Error: Failed to attach to process 21437: CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED (999)
Detail: cuptiActivityEnable() failed
```
Sam: When I launched the same workload with nsys profile (i.e. start process via nsys) it worked, but the timeline looked weird — lots of tiny kernel gaps and long memcpy stalls.
Alex: Does the container seccomp profile block ptrace/ioctl/perf_event_open? Attaching needs some syscalls. In our k8s private nodes we sandbox heavily.
Maria: Confirmed — our runtime seccomp blocks syscall 298/ioctl for some sandboxes. I saw IOCTL EPERM in dmesg when attach failed.
Sam: Example dmesg on host:
```
Mar  3 11:12:10 node kernel: audit: type=1327 audit(1610000000.123:456): proctitle=...
Mar  3 11:12:10 node kernel: security: audit: avc:  denied  { ioctl } for  pid=21437 comm="nsys" scontext=unconfined tcontext=unconfined tclass=chr_file
```
Priya: Interesting. I also saw a CUPTI handshake bug on certain driver + nsys combinations where cuptiActivityEnable fails on attach vs on-launch. Which nsys / driver did you use?
Sam: nsys 2024.1 (packaged via our infra image), NVIDIA driver 525.60.11, CUDA 12.1.
Alex: 525.x had a regression with CUPTI attach. Our infra notes say nsys 2023.8 + driver 525 sometimes works, but nsys 2024.x expects a newer CUPTI ABI that ships with driver 535+. Options: (1) upgrade driver to 535+ on repro nodes, (2) use older nsys for attach runs, or (3) run nsys by launching the process instead of attach.
Maria: Upgrade isn't trivial for customers in Private. We should try reproducing inside a non-sandboxed container first (CAP_SYS_PTRACE / --privileged) to isolate seccomp vs driver.
Sam: Did that. With --cap-add=SYS_PTRACE attach succeeds and trace looks valid — but perfetto kernel timeline still shows intermittent kernel preemption spikes tied to our memory-copy kernels. Snapshot from perfetto UI (condensed):
```
Kernel timeline: launch_kernel() [0.8ms] -> gpu_memcpy_async [3.5ms] -> idle gap [12ms] -> kernel_relaunch [0.9ms]
GPU occupancy drops during gap.
```
Sam: The gaps line up with threads on the host being scheduled away, and NVTX shows repeated small launches (we're doing small-batch hot loops).
Priya: Could be batching heuristic fallout: the runtime switched to the small-batch fast-path kernel (fp16-fused) that has higher kernel launch overhead at certain sequence lengths. When KV cache hits are low we call more kernels. Do you see more kernel launches per token?
Sam: Yes — per-token kernel count moved from ~2 -> ~6 on these traces. That multiplied launch overhead and exposed preemption. Also noticed increased KV cache eviction churn in logs.
Alex: Two angles — mitigate profiling/attach friction and fix perf regression:
- For profiling: when attach fails, try: add CAP_SYS_PTRACE, mount /sys/kernel/debug, ensure /proc/sys/kernel/yama/ptrace_scope=0 temporarily, and match nsys<>driver versions. Use `nsys profile --force-overwrite --trace=cuda,nvtx --sample=cpu` to get a launched trace if attach not possible.
- For the runtime: add a cooldown to batching heuristic so we favor fewer kernel launches (coalesce small batches, length-aware kernel selection), and tune KV cache eviction threshold to avoid churn.
Maria: Small note: in some environments CUPTI will fail when debugfs is not mounted because it expects certain debugfs entries for metrics. Mounting debugfs on host:/sys/kernel/debug fixed a different customer's attach problem.
nsys-bot: Known issue: nsys 2024.1 + driver 525.x -> CUPTI attach failures. See internal ticket INF-3187. Recommended temporary workaround: use nsys 2023.10 for attach.
Sam: Quick repro steps I used (works with --privileged):
```bash
# start container
docker run --gpus all --cap-add=SYS_PTRACE -it --rm redwood-runtime:0.9.5 /bin/bash
# inside container
python -m redwood.server --model gpt-13b &
nsys attach --pid $(pgrep -f redwood.server) --output /tmp/run.qdrep
```
Sam: When not privileged attach fails with CUPTI_ERROR_NOT_INITIALIZED.
Priya: Good evidence. For the immediate production mitigation we've reverted the small-batch kernel selector in 0.9.6-canary and rolled that to a fraction of hosts. That brought tail back to baseline in canary.
Alex: For the longer term:
- Add per-host profiler health checks that validate nsys attach works (and report which nsys/driver combo is present).
- Improve runtime batching fallback: if kernel launch rate > threshold, switch to coalescing path for X seconds.
- Add instrumentation to KV cache metrics so we can correlate evictions -> kernel launch counts.
Maria: I'll open an infra ticket to test driver 535 on a subset of nodes and run the attach matrix (nsys 2023.10, 2024.1) and report back.
Sam: Thanks — attaching the small qdrep + perfetto trace in the ticket. Also adding the short command-output that shows the ioctl EPERM when attach fails so infra can correlate seccomp rules.
Priya: Nice. One more ask — can we add a short runbook in eng-runtime that lists: attach prerequisites (CAP_SYS_PTRACE, debugfs, ptrace_scope), known working nsys<>driver pairs, and quick on-host commands to collect perfetto slices? Saves time next round.
Sam: Will draft and add to /docs/profiling/runbooks.md after infra confirms driver matrix.
Infra Bot: Created ticket INF-3299: test-driver-nsys-matrix. Assigned to Maria.
Maria: Assigned and scheduled, ETA EOD tomorrow for initial matrix.
Sam: Sweet. If anyone wants the raw traces ping me and I'll drop links. :thumbsup:
